new_sources.summary: Spiritual bypassing - using spirituality to avoid unresolved psychological difficulty - has been studied almost entirely in Western samples. This conceptual paper asks whether the construct travels to Indian contexts and proposes a culturally situated alternative. The method is immanent critique: existing formulations are examined against their own stated aims to identify the assumptions they must make; those assumptions are tested against evidence from Indian cultural psychology, gender socialization research, and the psychology of religion. Literature is identified through targeted searches across three domains and synthesized thematically. Three assumptions are problematic in this context
new_sources.title: Spiritual bypassing among Indian women: toward a culturally situated assessment framework.
